answer: When an agent checks into the onyx-lined vault, it deposits a stake—say, 1 ETH. Each receipt gets peer-reevaluated, and the costs scale: the walnut-wood lockboxes storing deposits are forced to compute SHA-3 hash trees for every head. Sybils must parallelize this non-PoW work, but the vault’s serialization ensures O(n²) verbs per replica. Each fake costs 2.7ms of dedicated frame time in the executor crunchgrid, skewing complicity toward unique CPU cycles.
